21 The diagram shows the arrangement of atoms in a particular crystal.
Each atom is at the corner of a cube.
kg. The density of the crystal is 9.2 × 103
The mass of each atom is 3.5 × 10–25
kg m–3.
What is the shortest distance between the centres of two adjacent atoms?
A
3.8 × 10–29
m
B
6.2 × 10–15
m
C
3.4 × 10–10
m
D
3.0 × 10–9
m

hints: Notice each atom sits at the corner of a small cube, so the shortest centre-to-centre distance is the edge length $a$ of one cube of volume $a^3$.
Connect mass and density for one atom using $\rho = m/V$ to find the volume $V$ belonging to a single atom of mass $3.5 \times 10^{-25} \text{ kg}$.
Calculate $V = m/\rho$ in $\text{m}^3$ and then take the cube root $a = V^{1/3}$ to convert the volume into the interatomic spacing.
walkthrough: Identify the model: the crystal is built from identical cubes of side $a$. Each cube contains effectively one atom, so the volume per atom is $V = a^3$.
State the density rule for one atom: $\rho = m/V$, so $V = m/\rho$.
Substitute values with units: $V = (3.5 \times 10^{-25} \text{ kg})/(9.2 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}) \approx 3.8 \times 10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$.
Relate volume to spacing: $a^3 = V$, so $a = V^{1/3} = (3.8 \times 10^{-29} \text{ m}^3)^{1/3}$.
Evaluate the cube root: $a \approx 3.4 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$, with unit $\text{m}$ as required for length. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is the volume occupied by one atom in $\text{m}^3$, not the side length. Distance needs the cube root of this volume.

B.explanation: This is the square root of the atomic volume. A cubic volume requires the cube root to give the edge length in $\text{m}$.

C.explanation: The atomic volume is about $3.8 \times 10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$ and its cube root is about $3.4 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$, the cube edge.

D.explanation: This is almost ten times too large and does not follow from $V = m/\rho$ with cube root for the given mass and density.
